title: Managing Shared Hospital Capacity for Medical Tourism: Patient Behavior and Hybrid Simulation (simulation model)
description:
A hybrid agent-based and discrete-event simulation, built in AnyLogic, of a multi-specialty international-patient hospital department that serves medical tourists and local patients from the same beds, specialists and appointment slots.

Patient behavior is part of the model's operating logic: medication adherence, physician switching, online versus in-person channel choice, and early abandonment all feed back into patient flow. The model also contains a daily bed-sharing routine for the compatible sections (cardiology, internal medicine and breast oncology); as implemented, this routine never adds beds (see the README). The discrete-event layer carries visits, hospitalization, recovery and re-presentation.

Across 30 hybrid and 36 discrete-event-only randomized-seed replications at a bed-constrained configuration, the hybrid model's mean inpatient admission waiting time is 14.8 days against 25.8 days in an otherwise identical discrete-event-only version (about 42 percent lower, p < 0.001), and the gap persists, at 25 to 64 percent, at higher demand and at larger bed counts. The difference is the combined effect of the patient-behavior mechanisms; the bed-sharing routine runs in both versions, so bed sharing is not evaluated. The behavior mechanisms also make abandonment and adherence-driven emergency escalation visible, which the discrete-event-only version omits. Neither version has been validated against observed waiting times.

Requires AnyLogic 8.9.8 (Personal Learning Edition or higher). An interactive web build runs on AnyLogic Cloud without installation.
